transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I lie there a long time at night trying to drift off, and then I wake up from bad dreams, or... or even just little noises. And once I'm awake, I just can't seem to settle back down.
Did this trouble sleeping start after any particular frightening, dangerous, or traumatic event happened to you?
Yes, it did. This has all been going on since... well, since I had a ladder accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now.
Since the accident, do you find yourself having sudden, vivid memories or flashbacks of the ladder accident during the day, even when you're not trying to think about it?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes, well... if I hear a piece of metal scrape, or maybe I just see a ladder leaning up in somebody's yard, the whole thing just jumps right back into my head. It's like I'm right back under there again, just waiting for help.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid places, activities, or reminders—like ladders or being up high—that bring back memories of what happened?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep finding reasons not to go down to the senior center, or even to work around my own garage anymore. I stay away from the tools, and especially that spot where I used to keep that ladder. I just don't want to be near it.
Since the accident, have you noticed a change in how you feel about yourself or others—like feeling more numb, distant from people, or persistently down, guilty, or fearful?

Yeah, I have noticed that. I feel kind of... distant, I guess. Like, my wife will be sitting right there, and the bridge fellows will be joking around, but I just feel like I'm behind a window. I'm in the room, but I'm not really with them, if that makes sense.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge or 'on guard,' or being easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yeah, I suppose I do. It's just... well, when I go places now, I find myself looking all around. I check up high to see if anything might fall, and I look for where the exits are. I even check if the floor or the steps look steady before I can finally sit down and feel easy about being there. I'm just always checking.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed a cluster of symptoms following a life-threatening ladder accident approximately 19 months ago, satisfying the criterion for exposure to a traumatic, life-threatening event. He reports intrusive re-experiencing (vivid flashbacks triggered by sensory cues like metal scraping or seeing ladders), persistent avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (avoiding the garage, tools, senior center), negative alterations in cognition/mood (emotional numbing, feeling detached from wife and friends), and marked hyperarousal/hypervigilance (constant scanning of environment, checking exits, hyperawareness of physical safety). Symptoms have persisted for well over one month (19 months), meeting duration criteria for chronic PTSD, and are causing functional/social impairment (withdrawal from senior center and hobbies, relational distancing). This symptom profile across all four PTSD symptom clusters, with chronicity beyond 3 months, supports a diagnosis of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (chronic) rather than Adjustment Disorder or Generalized Anxiety Disorder, which do not require a specific trauma exposure or the full symptom cluster pattern.
